topic: Commercial kitchen exhaust and make-up air in Ontario: practical coordination checks before permit submission

source_packet.title: O. Reg. 163/24: Building Code
source_packet.sourceCurrency: Benchmark research check: consolidated page reported last amendment O. Reg. 119/26 and adoption of NBC 2020 First Printing as amended by Ontario Amendments dated April 21, 2026.
facts: Ontario Regulation 163/24 is the current Building Code regulation framework used for this benchmark.
The regulation adopts the National Building Code of Canada 2020, First Printing, together with Ontario amendments.
The old O. Reg. 332/12 framework survives only for the regulation's stated transition cases; it must not be presented as the general current Ontario Building Code.

This source packet does not verify a specific commercial-kitchen exhaust airflow, make-up-air percentage, hood geometry, duct construction requirement, clearance, discharge separation, fire-suppression requirement, or clause/article number. Any such current-code claim requires current-code verification before publication.

source_packet.title: Ontario's Building Code
source_packet.sourceCurrency: Official Ontario Building Code information page available at benchmark preparation.
facts: Ontario directs users to the current Building Code Compendium and advises checking that the downloaded compendium is the latest version.
A high-level Ontario information page is not enough evidence for a detailed clause, airflow value, separation distance, or other numeric current-code requirement.

source_packet.title: ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 154-2022 - Ventilation for Commercial Cooking Operations
source_packet.sourceCurrency: ASHRAE titles, purposes and scopes page identified Standard 154-2022 as the published standard at benchmark preparation.
facts: ASHRAE identifies Standard 154-2022 as Ventilation for Commercial Cooking Operations.
Its stated purpose is to provide design criteria for the performance of commercial cooking ventilation systems.

This packet intentionally does not reproduce the standard text and does not establish any specific ASHRAE airflow rate, hood factor, replacement-air percentage, or mandatory design value. Specific requirements from the standard must not be invented.
